taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-04, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 4201.4 | 5.06 | 5.06
2 | 2238.9 | 4.35 | 9.41
3 | 343.9 | 31.91 | 41.32
4 | 25.0 | 0.99 | 42.31
5 | 10.9 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as H-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-04, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Note – Station T-04, Survey Area T**

The VES interpretation at T-04 resolves five layers. Resistivity decreases monotonically with depth: a resistive near-surface layer (4201.4 Ω·m, 0–5.06 m) is underlain by a second resistive layer (2238.9 Ω·m, to 9.41 m), then a moderate-resistivity layer (343.9 Ω·m, to 41.32 m), a low-resistivity layer (25.0 Ω·m, to 42.31 m), and a conductive basal layer (10.9 Ω·m).

Applying the curve-type convention to the three consecutive triplets (1-2-3, 2-3-4, 3-4-5), each shows r(n) > r(n+1) > r(n+2), i.e., a consistently decreasing resistivity sequence. This corresponds to Q-type (QQQ, simplified to Q), not H-type as recorded in the file. An H-type curve would require a resistivity decrease followed by an increase, which is not observed here. The on-file classification should be corrected to Q-type for consistency with the layer model.

{"curve_type_stated": "QQQ", "label_issue_flagged": true}
